In [[mathematics]], the '''incomplete Bessel functions''' are types of [[special function]]s which act as a type of extension from the complete-type of [[Bessel functions]].

==Definition==
The '''incomplete Bessel functions''' are defined as the same [[delay differential equation]]s of the complete-type [[Bessel functions]]:
:<math>J_{v-1}(z,w)-J_{v+1}(z,w)=2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}J_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>Y_{v-1}(z,w)-Y_{v+1}(z,w)=2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}Y_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>I_{v-1}(z,w)+I_{v+1}(z,w)=2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}I_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>K_{v-1}(z,w)+K_{v+1}(z,w)=-2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}K_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{v-1}^{(1)}(z,w)-H_{v+1}^{(1)}(z,w)=2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}H_v^{(1)}(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{v-1}^{(2)}(z,w)-H_{v+1}^{(2)}(z,w)=2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}H_v^{(2)}(z,w)</math>
And the following suitable extension forms of [[delay differential equation]]s from that of the complete-type [[Bessel functions]]:
:<math>J_{v-1}(z,w)+J_{v+1}(z,w)=\dfrac{2v}{z}J_v(z,w)-\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}J_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>Y_{v-1}(z,w)+Y_{v+1}(z,w)=\dfrac{2v}{z}Y_v(z,w)-\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}Y_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>I_{v-1}(z,w)-I_{v+1}(z,w)=\dfrac{2v}{z}I_v(z,w)-\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}I_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>K_{v-1}(z,w)-K_{v+1}(z,w)=-\dfrac{2v}{z}K_v(z,w)+\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}K_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{v-1}^{(1)}(z,w)+H_{v+1}^{(1)}(z,w)=\dfrac{2v}{z}H_v^{(1)}(z,w)-\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}H_v^{(1)}(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{v-1}^{(2)}(z,w)+H_{v+1}^{(2)}(z,w)=\dfrac{2v}{z}H_v^{(2)}(z,w)-\dfrac{2\tanh vw}{z}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial w}H_v^{(2)}(z,w)</math>
Where the new parameter <math>w</math> defines the integral bound of the '''upper-incomplete form''' and '''lower-incomplete form''' of the '''modified Bessel function of the second kind''':<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=D. S. |title=Incomplete Bessel functions. I |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |date=February 2007 |volume=50 |issue=1 |pages=173–183 |doi=10.1017/S0013091505000490 |doi-access = free }}</ref>
:<math>K_v(z,w)=\int_w^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh vt~dt</math>
:<math>J_v(z,w)=\int_0^we^{-z\cosh t}\cosh vt~dt</math>

==Properties==
:<math>J_v(z,w)=J_v(z)+\dfrac{e^\frac{v\pi i}{2}J(iz,v,w)-e^{-\frac{v\pi i}{2}}J(-iz,v,w)}{i\pi}</math>
:<math>Y_v(z,w)=Y_v(z)+\dfrac{e^\frac{v\pi i}{2}J(iz,v,w)+e^{-\frac{v\pi i}{2}}J(-iz,v,w)}{\pi}</math>
:<math>I_{-v}(z,w)=I_v(z,w)</math> for integer <math>v</math>
:<math>I_{-v}(z,w)-I_v(z,w)=I_{-v}(z)-I_v(z)-\dfrac{2\sin v\pi}{\pi}J(z,v,w)</math>
:<math>I_v(z,w)=I_v(z)+\dfrac{J(-z,v,w)-e^{-v\pi i}J(z,v,w)}{i\pi}</math>
:<math>I_v(z,w)=e^{-\frac{v\pi i}{2}}J_v(iz,w)</math>
:<math>K_{-v}(z,w)=K_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>K_v(z,w)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\dfrac{I_{-v}(z,w)-I_v(z,w)}{\sin v\pi}</math> for non-integer <math>v</math>
:<math>H_v^{(1)}(z,w)=J_v(z,w)+iY_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_v^{(2)}(z,w)=J_v(z,w)-iY_v(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{-v}^{(1)}(z,w)=e^{v\pi i}H_v^{(1)}(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_{-v}^{(2)}(z,w)=e^{-v\pi i}H_v^{(2)}(z,w)</math>
:<math>H_v^{(1)}(z,w)=\dfrac{J_{-v}(z,w)-e^{-v\pi i}J_v(z,w)}{i\sin v\pi}=\dfrac{Y_{-v}(z,w)-e^{-v\pi i}Y_v(z,w)}{\sin v\pi}</math> for non-integer <math>v</math>
:<math>H_v^{(2)}(z,w)=\dfrac{e^{v\pi i}J_v(z,w)-J_{-v}(z,w)}{i\sin v\pi}=\dfrac{Y_{-v}(z,w)-e^{v\pi i}Y_v(z,w)}{\sin v\pi}</math> for non-integer <math>v</math>

==Differential equations==
<math>K_v(z,w)</math> satisfies the inhomogeneous [[Bessel's differential equation]]
:<math>z^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dz^2}+z\dfrac{dy}{dz}-(x^2+v^2)y=(v\sinh vw+z\cosh vw\sinh w)e^{-z\cosh w}</math>
Both <math>J_v(z,w)</math> , <math>Y_v(z,w)</math> , <math>H_v^{(1)}(z,w)</math> and <math>H_v^{(2)}(z,w)</math> satisfy the [[partial differential equation]]
:<math>z^2\dfrac{\partial^2y}{\partial z^2}+z\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial z}+(z^2-v^2)y-\dfrac{\partial^2y}{\partial w^2}+2v\tanh vw\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial w}=0</math>
Both <math>I_v(z,w)</math> and <math>K_v(z,w)</math> satisfy the [[partial differential equation]]
:<math>z^2\dfrac{\partial^2y}{\partial z^2}+z\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial z}-(z^2+v^2)y-\dfrac{\partial^2y}{\partial w^2}+2v\tanh vw\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial w}=0</math>

==Integral representations==
Base on the preliminary definitions above, one would derive directly the following integral forms of <math>J_v(z,w)</math> , <math>Y_v(z,w)</math>:
:<math>\begin{align}
J_v(z,w)&=J_v(z)+\dfrac{1}{\pi i}\left(\int_0^we^{\frac{v\pi i}{2}-iz\cosh t}\cosh vt~dt-\int_0^we^{iz\cosh t-\frac{v\pi i}{2}}\cosh vt~dt\right)
\\&=J_v(z)+\dfrac{1}{\pi i}\left(\int_0^w\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt-i\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\right.\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\left.-\int_0^w\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt-i\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\right)
\\&=J_v(z)+\dfrac{1}{\pi i}\left(-2i\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\right)
\\&=J_v(z)-\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\end{align}</math>
:<math>\begin{align}
Y_v(z,w)&=Y_v(z)+\dfrac{1}{\pi}\left(\int_0^we^{\frac{v\pi i}{2}-iz\cosh t}\cosh vt~dt+\int_0^we^{iz\cosh t-\frac{v\pi i}{2}}\cosh vt~dt\right)
\\&=Y_v(z)+\dfrac{1}{\pi}\left(\int_0^w\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt-i\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\right.\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\left.+\int_0^w\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt+i\int_0^w\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\right)
\\&=Y_v(z)+\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^w\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt\end{align}</math>
With the Mehler–Sonine integral expressions of <math>J_v(z)=\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt</math> and <math>Y_v(z)=-\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt</math> mentioned in [[Digital Library of Mathematical Functions]],<ref>{{dlmf|id=10.9.8|title=Bessel Functions|first=R. B. |last=Paris}}</ref>

we can further simplify to <math>J_v(z,w)=\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_w^\infty\sin\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt</math> and <math>Y_v(z,w)=-\dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_w^\infty\cos\left(z\cosh t-\dfrac{v\pi}{2}\right)\cosh vt~dt</math> , but the issue is not quite good since the convergence range will reduce greatly to <math>|v|<1</math>.
